{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-09-28: "I just want to review the reflow2 code and make sure we're not straying/drifting from its core identity (and if possible, look at ways to improve how it delivers on its core identity)." The yardstick is req:no-se-knowledge: "The graph carries the discipline; the user answers plain questions."

WHAT IS ALREADY ON THE RECORD: the 2026-09-13 spirit review (epoch:2026-09-13-all-of-reflow-read-back-for-its-spirit-and-intent; fact:reflow2-keeps-reflows-spirit-and-inherits-its-one-real-drift) compared reflow2 with the ORIGINAL reflow's spirit. It did not ask the narrower question here: at each point where a person meets reflow2, does it ask them for systems-engineering knowledge they don't have?

WAYS THE REVIEW COULD BE RUN, NONE CHOSEN (cheapest first):
(a) WALK IT AS A NON-ENGINEER. Run genesis, then the gaps, a build and a change, as a person who knows no systems engineering, through a chat app and through Claude Code. Count every place reflow2 LEAKS:
  - a node type or edge name shown to the person;
  - a question only an engineer could answer;
  - a refusal that needs design-practice knowledge to act on;
  - a reply too long to read.
  The product is a leak list, each leak a finding. It measures the identity directly, and it is small (hours, agent-run with a persona). Earlier genesis trials (bhome, musicjug, usgov) are evidence of this kind already on the record.
(b) CLASSIFY THE SURFACE BY WHO IT SERVES. Tag every served tool, skill and detector as serving the designer, the agent on the designer's behalf, reflow2's own upkeep, or hosting operators. That shows how much of the surface serves the identity. Medium; mostly mechanical over the toolsnaps and skills.
(c) READ THE CODE MODULE BY MODULE for features no path a person takes ever reaches; req:the-design-says-what-was-built-and-never-used is the accepted instrument for this. Large, because the crates are big: the most effort, and the least direct measure of the identity.
(d) A STANDING CHECK, so drift cannot come back quietly: every new tool or skill names, in a person's words, which plain question it answers or which leak it closes. The find_tools corpus already holds one query per tool in a user's words; this extends it. Small to add, but only useful once (a) or (b) says what the core is.

IMPROVEMENTS THE REVIEW WOULD FEED (named, not evaluated):
- how plain gap_to_prompt's questions are;
- whether the lens's vocabulary swap reaches every reply;
- the human-readable view the original reflow made blocking and reflow2 still lacks (SV-1/SV-4, epoch:the-systems-views-are-rendered-from-the-graph).

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
· Reading the CODE measures what the builder intended, not what a person experiences. The identity lives in what a person SEES, so (a) is closer to it than (c).
· The 2026-09-13 review already found the drift, and little of it was acted on. A second review risks producing another report, which is reflow's own drift ("NEVER generate reports"). Any review is worth pairing with a decision on what gets parked or fixed.
· The agent, not the engine, is the translator: an LLM hides systems-engineering vocabulary well or badly depending on the skills and the replies it is given. So a review has to cover the agent's side (skills, served instructions, reply shapes), not only the Rust.
